newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf rigs down in the week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf rigs down in the week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 965 as of Thursday, down one from the prior week and 183 above the year-ago total of 782, Baker Hughes Inc. reported Monday.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by two to 818, while rigs working offshore remained at 122. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose one to 25.
Among individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which was up by four and California and Wyoming, which were both down by three.
The Gulf of Mexico rig count remained at 118.
A total of 380 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down 12 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 11 to 583, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at two.
There were 214 rigs drilling directionally, 67 drilling horizontally and 684 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 14 to 335, versus 275 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 166 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Monday, down one from the period ending June 27.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 175, was 94.9 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area was unchanged at 110 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 113, a utilization rate unchanged at 97.3 pct.
The worldwide rig count was also unchanged at 576 out of a total fleet of 604, with an unchanged utilization rate of 95.4 percent.
